stance_text: Watch — unchanged, bias now neutral; fair value lowered from $288.98 (FY2031) to $109.41 (end-2029), 10.4% a year from $81.31 (Own at about $72). Contract terms improved, but a third of Q3 revenue was one-off partnership revenue, receivables quintupled, delivery slipped two months, 2027 capex is $40-45B at about $40M per MW, and the bear, at 35% weight, leaves the equity worth nothing
lens_text: End-2029 value: 2030 adjusted EBITDA (megawatts billing x revenue per MW x margin) times an exit EV/EBITDA (5.0x / 6.0x / 7.5x), less end-2029 net debt rolled forward from September 30 with unrestricted cash (capex at $40-42M per MW added, half paid a year ahead and the 2030 capacity fully paid by end-2029; cash coupons on the convertibles plus 7.0-9.0% on the rest of the average balance; VIE advances; receivables to 45 days; deferred-revenue inflows; equity raised; convertibles that convert above conversion price x accretion), less 75% of end-2029 deferred revenue, plus $1.60B of equity stakes at book, over end-2029 shares with 1.5% a year of stock-comp dilution; equity floored at zero; three-year value, undiscounted

bear.basis: Pricing resets toward $10.5-11.5M per MW and the build stops near 1.55 GW by end-2029 (0.6 GW added in 2027 against the >1 GW plan); 2027 revenue $9.0B against the $12-13B outlook; 2030 revenue $16.8B at 42% ($7.06B EBITDA) x 5.0x = $35.3B EV, below $42.0B of end-2029 net debt after $53.6B of capex from Q4 2026 ($42M per MW added), 9% interest on non-convertible debt and $8B of equity sold near $35; 562.6M shares; equity floored at zero

base.basis: 0.75 / 0.8 / 0.7 GW added in 2027-29 (below the >1 GW a year plan) to 2.6 GW billing, 0.5 GW more in 2030; blended revenue per MW $17.0M falling to $14.5M as hyperscaler capacity and repriced older GPUs mix in; 2027 revenue $12.3B (low end of the outlook); 2030 revenue $41.3B at 50% ($20.66B EBITDA) x 6.0x = $124.0B; end-2029 net debt $67.6B after $96.6B of capex from Q4 2026 at $40M per MW plus the $10B balance of the 2030 capacity, convertible coupons plus 7.5% on the rest of the average balance, receivables at 45 days, $8B of equity at about $90 and conversion of the June 2025 notes (3.5M shares); 75% of $24B deferred revenue deducted; $1.6B stakes; 426.4M shares

bull.basis: About 1 GW a year delivered at near-today's pricing ($18.5M falling to $17.5M per MW) to 3.3 GW billing by end-2029; 2030 revenue $64.4B at 56% ($36.06B EBITDA) x 7.5x = $270.5B; end-2029 net debt $66.6B after $125.6B of capex at $40M per MW plus $16B for the rest of the 2030 capacity, convertible coupons plus 7% on the rest, every convertible series converting (68.2M shares) and $6B of equity at about $180; 75% of $32B deferred revenue deducted; 435.6M shares

deviation_from_street.reason: The bear and the cost of the build: we give 35% weight to a case in which enterprise value at 5.0x 2030 EBITDA is below end-2029 net debt and the equity is worth nothing, charge about $40M of capex per MW added (including all of the 2030 capacity the forward EBITDA counts), and deduct 75% of customer prepayments, on which Nebius itself accretes interest, as debt-like. Street targets are 12-month prices and our value is at end-2029, so the horizon gap runs the other way; the base alone ($93.84) is 59% below the mean.

thesis: Q3 confirmed demand and improved deal terms (ACV above $25M per MW, payback 1y7m, prepayments above 100% of associated capex, $12B of new contract value, Databricks, Datadog and Snowflake signed), but a third of revenue ($325.1M) was one-off asset-light partnership revenue, receivables jumped to $4.04B (75% one customer), third-party capacity slipped into H1 2027, and 2027 capex of $40-45B came in about $14B above Street models. The stock fell 47% in seven sessions with the whole neocloud group, to $81.31. On end-2029 values of $0 / $93.84 / $416.59 at 35/50/15 the weighted value is $109.41, 10.4% a year: Watch. The base is 6.0x 2030 EBITDA but about 67x EBIT, because five-year GPU depreciation consumes most of the EBITDA of a fleet still growing fast, so the equity is a levered claim on 2028-2030 GPU pricing, on capex per MW, and on funding $6-11B a year outside prepayments. Own at about $72.
consensus_view: Twenty-two analysts (S&P Global, November 16) rate the stock Buy on balance with a $231.60 mean target ($84-$380), cut from $281 in October; Citi ($215), Truist ($245), Bank of America ($265) and Northland ($380) kept Buy, D.A. Davidson cut to $125 at Hold. Consensus revenue is $3.16B for FY2026 and $12.36B for FY2027, with non-GAAP EPS of -$1.12 and -$3.04. The market disagrees with the Street: the stock is down 72% from its June 18 record and 47% since the Q3 report, trading with CoreWeave and IREN on fears that debt-funded AI capacity outruns demand, after Nvidia's CEO departure and a failed lift from Anthropic's IPO.
variant_view: No variant view on price: at $81.31 the weighted value is 10.4% a year, and we share the market's fear of the bear at 35% weight. Our disagreement is with the Street, whose $231.60 mean target is 2.1x our value. On our build, base 2030 EBIT is about $1.8B on $124B of EV (about 67x) and pre-tax income is still negative, because five-year GPU depreciation consumes most of the EBITDA of a fleet bought at about $40M per MW; owner earnings do not support Street-style EBITDA multiples until the build slows. Checkable: Q4 2026 revenue excluding strategic-partnership revenue below $900M (0.55), which would show Q3's beat was the one-off and the Q4 guide leans on more of it.

notes: The October call was a backfill whose values were FY2031 EV/EBITDA values; this update states end-2029 values, undiscounted, on 2030 adjusted EBITDA, as the November IREN update does. Discounted at the initiation's 12.28% for three years, $109.41 at end-2029 is about $77 today, 52% below October's discounted $161.95. The value fell a little further than the price.

Net debt starts at September 30 debt principal of $16,478.0M (convertible notes at their accreted maturity amounts plus the $751.8M MUFG term loan) less $7,425.6M of unrestricted cash; $1,215.5M of restricted cash is excluded. Q4 2026 adds about $11.6B of capex (FY2026 about $27B less $15.43B in nine months), $0.9B of VIE note advances and a quarter's interest (convertible cash coupons of about $263M a year, plus the case rate on the rest of net debt; the notes' accretion is already in the $16,478.0M), less Q4 adjusted EBITDA of about $374M (36% on about $1.04B of Q4 revenue). The $3.5B Citi facility and lease liabilities are not added: drawn proceeds fund capex already counted, and site leases sit inside cost of revenue and EBITDA.

Capex is MW added times $40M (bear $42M) all-in, half paid in the year before the MW bills, and the rest of the 2030 additions is charged by end-2029 (base $10B, bull $16B), so the forward EBITDA is fully paid for. The $40M follows from the guide: $40-45B of 2027 capex 'sized for more than 1 GW', including owned-site shells, power and pre-build. The letter's payback of 1y7m 'on a revenue basis' at ACV above $25M per MW implies roughly $20-22M of GPU and fit-out capex per MW on Q3 deals, excluding the shell; at $35M per MW the fair value is $131.01 (17.2%), at $45M $87.73 (2.6%). The base's 2027 capex of $31B is below the guide because it adds 0.75 GW, not more than 1 GW.

Receivables were $4,039.9M at September 30 (from $720.3M at December 31), 75% from one customer (Customer D); Q3 operating cash flow was -$273.0M although deferred revenue rose $3.43B, which suggests invoiced prepayments not yet collected. The model collects them and holds receivables at 45 days of revenue by end-2029. The adjustment is applied at end-2029, outside the interest roll-forward; collecting earlier would add less than $1 a share.

Deferred revenue ($9.41B at September 30) rises in a straight line to $14B / $24B / $32B at end-2029 and counts as a cash inflow; 75% of the end-2029 balance is deducted from equity value because Nebius treats the prepayments as carrying a significant financing component and accretes interest on them ($121.1M in nine months 2026). Deducting 50% or 100% moves the fair value to $119.20 or $99.60. The end-2029 balances are assumptions, not derived from the $17-20B of 2027 prepayments guided less a recognition schedule, which Nebius does not give.

A convertible series converts when the case's end-2029 value is above its conversion price times its accretion ratio: June 2025 notes $51.45 (about $178.7M original, accreting to $214.4M), September 2025 notes $138.75 (115%, break-even about $159.56), March 2026 notes $183.22 and $180.31 (120%), August 2026 notes $313.46 (110%) and $324.65 (125%). Shares start at 319.46M (292.90M outstanding, 21.07M NVIDIA pre-funded warrants, 5.49M unvested RSUs) and grow 1.5% a year from stock compensation ($196.5M in nine months 2026).

Cross-check on depreciation (five-year GPU life on 65% of gross PP&E, 20 years on the rest): base 2030 D&A about $18.8B, EBIT about $1.8B (EV/EBIT about 67x at 6.0x EBITDA), pre-tax about -$2.3B. Exit EV per average MW billing in 2030 is about $43.5M in the base, roughly replacement cost. The bull's EV/EBIT is about 22x; the bear's EBIT is negative. Management's Q4 2027 pre-tax breakeven needs better pricing, lower capex per MW or slower growth than the base.

Sensitivities at 35/50/15 (all printed by the script): base exit 5.5x $97.29 (6.2% a year), 7.0x $133.64 (18.0%); every case at 10% on non-convertible debt $105.75 (9.2%); capex $35M per MW $131.01 (17.2%), $45M $87.73 (2.6%); base revenue per MW -$1M $97.08, -$2M $84.67; base 2030 margin 46% gives a base of $70.58; $15B of base equity at $50 gives a base of $75.03; weights 30/50/20 $130.24 (17.0%), 40/45/15 $104.72, 40/50/10 $88.58 (2.9%). The base exit multiple that returns $81.31 is about 5.7x. The bull carries $62.49 of the $109.41; without it (bear and base reweighted) the value is $55.20. Own needs a price at or below about $71.94. The weights: the bull keeps 15%, not 10%, because Q3 deal terms (ACV above $25M per MW, prepayments above 100% of capex) are bull-case terms today; it rises to 20% only if Q4 shows recurring revenue at or above $1.0B and RPO at or above $50B.

Recurring Q3 margin: if the $325.1M of partnership revenue carried no cost, AI cloud adjusted EBITDA on the other $648.7M of AI cloud revenue was $193.1M (29.8%); if it carried half its revenue in cost, 54.8%. The 6-K does not disclose its cost.

Starting capacity (300 / 350 / 380 MW billing at end-2026) and revenue per MW are fitted to the FY2026 guide and the $12-13B FY2027 outlook; Nebius discloses no active-MW figure in the text of the letter, and its capacity charts (images) were not read.

Base rates: all three revenue paths (77%, 127%, 156% a year from $3.0B) are above the 99th percentile for companies starting at $1.5-3B; Nebius is building a business, not growing one. capital.multiples gives no usable check: 20-F annual facts only, and SIC 7370 peers are software companies.
Nebius reports quarters on 6-K, which data/calendar/earnings.csv (8-K Item 2.02) does not record, so library/CALENDAR.md did not flag this update as due.

Review round 1 (agent:reviewing-research, grade C): the first draft rated Own at $150.20 (22.7% a year). It charged no capex for 2030 additions that the forward EBITDA counted, treated $4.04B of receivables and $1.22B of restricted cash as cash, charged 6.0-7.5% on opening balances, had no stock-comp dilution, ignored accretion in the conversion test, deducted 50% of prepayments without reason, set claims that contradicted the weights, and never tested the 6.0x exit against cash returns. Fixed: capex at $40-42M per MW with half a year's lead, unrestricted cash, receivables to 45 days, average balances at 7.0-9.0%, 1.5% a year of dilution, conversion against accreted principal, 75% of prepayments deducted, claims realigned, a margin kill criterion, EV/EBIT and per-MW cross-checks. Fair value $121.82, Watch.

Review round 2 (grade B): half of the 2030 capacity was still unpaid at end-2029; the case rate was charged on convertibles already carried at their accreted amounts; the margin kill line (35% in any quarter) sat inside the base path; $40M per MW was unsourced; the 46% margin sensitivity did not reproduce; stale text in the projection and inputs. Fixed: the rest of the 2030 capacity charged by end-2029, convertibles charged their cash coupons, kill line at 30% (or 35% for two quarters), capex per MW derived from the guide with $35M / $45M sensitivities, all sensitivities printed by the script, text corrected. Fair value $109.41 (10.4% a year), bias moved to neutral.

low_score_reasons: valuation: The capex fix was half done: 2030 EBITDA counts every MW added in 2030, but only half of 2030's additions were charged before end-2029 ($10B base, $16B bull uncharged). Separately, the 7.0-9.0% rate was applied to convertibles already carried at their accreted maturity amounts ($15.73B, about 1.8% cash coupon), double-counting accretion. The two errors push in opposite directions, so the Own threshold was not reliable.

variant_view: The call says plainly it has no variant view on price; its only disagreement is with the Street's multiple, and the single checkable item (Q4 revenue excluding partnerships below $900M at 0.55) is close to a coin flip.

calibration: All three revenue paths are above the 99th percentile, the 35/50/15 weights are argued only in words, and the bull carries over half the value (bear and base alone are below the price). Claims are now consistent with the weights.
review.counter_case: The case for Own: the model is conservative where it counts. Management's own figures (ACV above $25M per MW, 1 year 7 months payback on a revenue basis covering opex and capex) imply capex of roughly $20-22M per MW on Q3 deals, against the $40M the model charges; at $35M the value clears the Own line. With prepayments now covering more than 100% of the associated capex, the 35% bear that wipes out the equity is a credit scenario the funding mix is designed to avoid. On that reading $81.31 is a mispricing, and Watch-and-wait is a distinction without a difference.
review.response: Accepted from round 2: the rest of the 2030 capacity is now charged by end-2029 and the convertibles carry their cash coupons (about $263M a year) with the case rate only on the rest of net debt; together they lower the fair value to $109.41 (10.4% a year), and Own now needs about $72. The margin kill criterion moved to below 30% in any 2027 quarter or below 35% in two consecutive quarters; the $40M per MW is derived from the $40-45B 2027 guide for more than 1 GW, with $35M ($131.01, 17.2%) and $45M ($87.73, 2.6%) printed; every sensitivity is now printed by the script; the stale projection and inputs text is fixed; the deferred-revenue path is labelled an assumption; the bull's 15% is tied to Q3 deal terms with a 20% trigger. On the counter-case we keep Watch: the payback figure covers GPUs and fit-out on one quarter's deals, not the owned-site shells, power and pre-build the 2027 guide pays for, and prepayments above 100% apply to Q3's new deals, not to the $6-11B a year of 2027 capex Nebius says falls outside prepayments and investment-grade financing, which is what a 364-day bridge and a tighter credit market put at risk. The bias moves to neutral; capex evidence near $35M per MW, a price near $72, or Q4 recurring revenue of $1.0B with RPO of $50B would move the call to Own.
